tagline: From the Roanoke River up to the Peaks of Otter.
intro: Route 43 leaves Altavista by way of Lynch Station and bends southwest along the north bank of the Roanoke River to Leesville, a little above the lake the river was dammed to make, then follows Goose Creek into Bedford County. Past Gillespie the road's street name is simply Virginia Byway.

It winds through Bedford, crosses the Otter River on Peaks Road and climbs into the Jefferson National Forest, ending at the Blue Ridge Parkway by the Peaks of Otter. Route 24, the Colonial Highway, belongs to the same byway and comes in at Gillespie from US 29 by way of Evington.

moments.title: Altavista
moments.text: The Lane brothers planned a town called Lane's Siding where the railroad they were building met the Southern, and on September 9, 1907 the first settlers arrived in a small red caboose.

moments.title: Bedford
moments.text: Bedford, home of the National D-Day Memorial, lost more residents per capita in the Normandy landings than any other American community.

moments.title: Peaks of Otter
moments.text: Thomas Jefferson wrote that these peaks were thought the tallest in the country measured from their base, and Virginia sent their stones to the Washington Monument before that turned out not to be so.
